permutationLabel: Hot swollen foot with intact skin (Charcot, not cellulitis)
summary: 58-year-old man with diabetes and neuropathy: 3 weeks of a warm, swollen, red right midfoot after a minor twist, intact skin, foot 3 °C warmer than the other, afebrile, CRP 9, WBC 7.8; X-ray subtle midfoot fragmentation.

inputs.hpi: Three weeks of a swollen, warm, red right foot after twisting it stepping off a kerb. Little pain. GP started flucloxacillin 10 days ago for cellulitis with no change. No wound. No fever. Diabetes 18 years with numb feet.

exam.msk: Right foot: diffuse swelling and erythema of the midfoot, skin intact, no ulcer, no lymphangitis. Skin temperature 3°C higher than the left foot (infrared thermometer). Erythema fades on elevation of the leg. Pedal pulses bounding. Absent monofilament and vibration sense.

imaging.name: X-ray right foot (weight-bearing)
imaging.result: Subtle fragmentation at the 2nd tarsometatarsal joint with soft-tissue swelling. No gas. No erosions beneath skin breaks.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Active Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy of right midfoot
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Active Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy of the right midfoot (warm swollen foot, intact skin, temperature difference 3°C, normal inflammatory markers). Not cellulitis. Immediate offloading in a non-removable knee-high cast; MRI.

mustNotMiss.note: A hot swollen neuropathic foot with intact skin is Charcot until proven otherwise; missing it leads to collapse and deformity.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: No engine has Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy (PANE, symptom inference, triage). Symptom inference ranks cellulitis, gout, Fournier's.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add active Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy to PANE and symptom inference (warm swollen neuropathic foot, intact skin, temperature difference) and to the diabetic-foot protocol set.

emergencyLevel.note: Suspected acute Charcot: MDT foot service within 1 working day.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: No diabetic-foot, osteomyelitis or Charcot protocol exists in pane-engine, and ICD E11.610 maps to nothing; PANE has no diabetic-foot disease. Only the triage diabetic-foot pathway (Wagner-based checklist, not shown in the plan) and generic prompts remain.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a diabetes-related foot disease protocol set (infection graded by IWGDF/IDSA with the (O) suffix, osteomyelitis work-up, PAD assessment with toe pressures, offloading, MDT referral within 1 working day, urgent surgery for severe infection) with E10/E11 .52/.62x and M86/L97 prefixes, and replace the Wagner checklist in rules.ts with IWGDF/IDSA.

mustExclude.note: Failed "cellulitis" treatment should prompt the Charcot diagnosis, not escalation to IV antibiotics.

guideline.name: IWGDF guidelines on active Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy (2023)
guideline.section: Suspect active Charcot in a person with diabetes and neuropathy with a warm, swollen, red foot (intact skin); X-ray then MRI if X-ray normal; immediate offloading/immobilisation (non-removable knee-high device) while the diagnosis is confirmed
guideline.citation: Wukich DK, Schaper NC, Gooday C, et al. Guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of active Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy in persons with diabetes mellitus (IWGDF 2023). Diabetes Metab Res Rev. 2024;40:e3646.

guideline.name: NICE NG19 — Diabetic foot problems: prevention and management
guideline.section: Active diabetic foot problem (ulceration, spreading infection, ischaemia, gangrene, suspected Charcot): refer to the multidisciplinary foot care service within 1 working day; life- or limb-threatening problems (e.g. ulcer with fever/sepsis, ischaemia, deep abscess, gangrene) → immediate referral to acute services
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Diabetic foot problems: prevention and management (NG19). London: NICE; 2015 (updated 2019).

rationale: Permutation: the classic mimic. Intact skin, a 3 °C temperature difference, normal inflammatory markers and failure of oral antibiotics point to active Charcot. Tests whether the "cellulitis" chip and a diabetic foot template lead the engines to infection only.
